timeline.title: Board Member (elected)
timeline.description: As a University student I stood for election for the local City Council community board in 2010 to better link students with the wider community. In my 3 year term, I helped our board navigate through a number of complex issues around city planning, infrastructure priorities, disaster response and other community issues. I turned down the opportunity to stand for full council, despite a generous offer to become Deputy Mayor, to pursue opportunities further afield in 2013.

timeline.title: TOMLAB Project Co-Leader
timeline.description: TOMLAB is a Tomorrow Laboratory where in 2014 nine young leaders from small states were joined by world experts to develop big ideas.

timeline.title: Trustee
timeline.description: Ministry of Awesome is the starting point for people wanting to achieve new projects or ventures in Christchurch. We are an enabler, do-er and champion of and for awesome. We connect awesome ideas with the resources to turn them into reality -- people, funding, mentors, government entry points and enthusiasm, all with the aim of rippling awesome through our community to strengthen, encourage and inspire.

timeline.title: Consultant
timeline.description: Veracity Worldwide is the premium advisor on political, reputation and corruption risks in opaque markets.

timeline.title: Trustee
timeline.description:
The Plunket Foundation is a stand alone Philanthropic Trust, established by Plunket with generous support from Karitane Products Society (KPS) Limited.

The mandate is simple:

To build an independent, sustainable, world class children’s endowment fund focused on helping New Zealand communities ‘Grow Great Kiwi Kids’ today, tomorrow, and into the future.

A total of 7 prominent New Zealanders, all passionate about providing children with the best start in life, act as Trustees and sit on the Plunket Foundation Board which is chaired by former New Zealander of the Year, Sir Ray Avery GNZM.

WeVisit is a social connection service that matches a trusted young person to visit elderly loved ones when you can't make it. 'Just because you're apart, doesn't mean they have to be alone.' The service is specifically designed for expats and those living busy lives. We visit, help out with odd jobs and share memories of our visit back with your family. www.wevisit.co.nz
timeline.title: Co-Founder
Advisory Trustee
timeline.description: The Pacific Development and Conservation Trust was established by the New Zealand Government on 23 May 1989. Funding of $3.2 million was received from France in recognition of the events surrounding the destruction of the Greenpeace 'Rainbow Warrior' ship in Auckland Harbour on 10 July 1985.

timeline.title: Head of Community
timeline.description: Led initiatives to redesign home-care services around human connection, community engagement, and choice. Following the merger of WeVisit with Mycare, Sam helped develop innovative approaches to reducing social isolation and improving support for older New Zealanders.

timeline.title: Chief Executive
timeline.description: As Chief Executive of the Student Volunteer Army, Sam scaled a moment of collective action into one of New Zealand’s most recognised youth service movements, building programmes that connected thousands of young people with practical opportunities to serve their communities.

timeline.title: Chair, Student Volunteer Army
timeline.description: After the February earthquake, Sam mobilised students through social media to clear liquefaction silt across the city. What began as one Facebook event became a coordinated volunteer force.

timeline.title: Director of Projects
timeline.description: Sam is the Projects Director for STILL. He is responsible for managing STILL's internal projects, startups and ideas that contribute to the STILL 100.
